items.text: PHP2Shell, day four, evening: nothing new. Still no organization confirmed breached by name; CISA's exploited-vulnerabilities catalog, opened directly, still has no PHP entry; no PHP release since Oct 21. Reuters: Cloudflare's Matthew Prince says he knows of 'a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities' in other critical software, and VulnCheck finds AI helped double disclosed flaws year on year.

New to the index: Straiker says the criminal group CyberCartel ran Claude- and Grok-driven agents against more than 400 Latin American banks and fintechs. Its stolen database held 4,493 records, among them 903 account numbers and 67 cleartext passwords. Anthropic revoked the credential; xAI is looking into it. One vendor's evidence, no victim named.

Also new: Reuters established that one Chinese-speaking hacker's AI agents, run through the open-source Cairn platform, broke into websites of more than 100 companies, Deere, SharkNinja and Cummins among them, at about $50 a hack. Deere says it has no indication sensitive information was accessed. Missed by this index for five days.

Johns Hopkins Bayview is telling 3,182 patients that a worker uploaded their names, treatment dates, medications and record numbers to a public AI tool the hospital had not approved. Discovered Sept 21, letters out Oct 22, tool unnamed. Two days after Panasonic's 334,000-person version of the same mistake.
